finding.gap: ClayVerseEngine rebuilt the derived ClayGraph only after canonical completion and active_turn retirement. If that rebuild raised after a verified effect had already been durably re-entered, ingest could report failure after the replay fence was gone, making caller retry semantics ambiguous and potentially duplicating a real effect.
finding.why_material: ClayGraph is rebuildable projection only. A projection failure must not erase or outlive the canonical active-turn fence around an already re-entered effect.
finding.strongest_counterhypothesis: Because ClayGraph is derived, projection failure should eventually be decoupled from canonical turn success entirely via an explicit durable projection-dirty/rebuild contract rather than blocking completion.
finding.counterhypothesis_disposition: DEFER. The existing Engine already surfaced graph rebuild failure as ingest failure. This repair preserves that fail-closed observable behavior while moving the failure before replay-fence retirement; it does not invent a second graph/state authority. A future fail-open projection contract requires its own explicit state/recovery design and evidence.

repair.mechanism: Use ClayGraphProjection.rebuild_in_tx() inside the existing completion/finalization transaction before workspace COMPLETED and active_turn deletion on both no-effect and effect paths; remove the trailing separate self.graph.rebuild().

cases: no-effect graph failure rolls completion back while keeping admitted active turn recoverable
post-effect graph failure preserves one VERIFIED effect plus matching causal re-entry, keeps active retry fence, rejects a second ingest, and lets Recovery close without a second effect
